Played the Demo and really enjoyed it, along with the classic rougelite aspects the tower defense actaully makes it stand out unlike a lot of the copy/paste rougelites out there, i highly recommend getting it and building the death machine of your dreams xD

If CleanFall doesn't blow up to be the next big roguelike I don't know what will. I truly think this is the next big roguelike like Noita or Spelunky and if it's not then I still think it's easily one of my favorite roguelikes I've played this year! It combines turret shenanigans with Terraria mining and exploration and an extremely unique tone and atmosphere. https://youtu.be/XmNUUEuebCg
非常好游戏
很好玩 我的战争机器一路创创创

草，【开路器会摧毁你光标正下方的目标】，尼玛开局新手教程多写几个字能死吗？刚出门让我用开路器，上面的土层红激光一键瞄准消了，然后掉到下面那个逼棍子上，怎么用红光消逼用都没有都射不穿，站在棍子上消不了，站在方块上消不了，往左右两边土层也开不了，往上跳几把跳不出去，这个逼开路器每次用还得等五秒，偏偏棍子左边那个方块用鼠标左键攻击还会发几把光，我还以为要用左键和开路器怎么联合，搞了逼十分钟，几把上网找教程因为是新游戏，只有2月份的教程，里面开局还几把没有这个开路器的部分，在这里耗了几把十五分钟，才踏马看到你要把光标放到这根几把棍子上，多写几个字能死吗？？或者你多给几个目标啊？要不然给个视频教程呢？本来我对【抢先体验游戏】的判断就是【半成品】，从来都不玩半成品给自己找窝囊气，但很喜欢noita，看评测视频也很有趣，所以开放能买了就觉得试试吧，结果玩个几把游戏新手教程卡十五分钟，我特么有个几把心情玩几把游戏啊

画风很有特色，游戏类型和noita比较类似，不过这个游戏的地图是随机生成的，带一点肉鸽要素，但都挺难的。主要是开局没有什么指引，不知道怎么做build提升强度。第一把的时候我连控制炮台都弄不明白，然后就一个劲往下挖到1800多m，中间午夜刷怪了就整几个炮塔防身。这里不得不说那个推进器是真的少。然后当然被1800m那个门刷的怪干死了。第二局稍微明白了一点，然后选了开局送推进器和炮台那个，这波比较顺得推到1800m，但还是打不过，那波的怪非常非常多。第三把的时候我才发现原来炮台是可以合成升级的，但是只能升二级（这玩意还是我不经意间发现的，几乎没有什么指引），升三级不知道是要局外成长还是要局内进入一定深度。这一把因为炮台形状没做好被一波带走了。 有几个很想吐槽的，一是这个炮台实在是太笨重了，如果做大一点，那就几乎没办法进入左右的墙体获得资源，因为地图上有很多不能破坏的东西，炮台被这玩意卡柱就动不了了。如果做小了午夜根本撑不住那么多怪。几种炮台里，机枪塔看着特效很足，但是感觉他启动延迟太高，经常还没输出就被蹭掉一点血；火焰塔稍微好一点点，但是手非常短也容易被蹭。这里墙体的重要性就体现出来了，然而又回到上面的问题，你放了墙体来保护炮台，那么炮台必然会做的很大，这时候你就很难补充资源。然后有一个组合炮台，就是机枪和藤蔓好像，可以组合出一个青蛙炮台，这玩意纯纯就是坑自己的，他不能跟着炮台走，而且刷出来的青蛙要是掉进你的炮台缝隙里都抠都抠不出来，硬占你炮台的空间，我感觉是一个纯负面的东西。 然后是炮台阵型的调整，游戏特地限制了炮台抓取力度，很多稍微大一点点的都是动不了的，其实这样弄感觉非常难受，因为你不太可能一开始就完全规划好炮台的组件，往往是抓到什么就补什么，就会做出来一个非常丑也非常畸形的炮台，很可能怪就从哪个缝隙进来给你偷一滴血。理想的组合状态就是左上、右上、正下放地图上抓来的陨石，用墙体连接起来，正上方开口，用两个火焰炮台做一个电锯。这样方便进出，怪也不会冲进来。内部就装推进器，挖掘核心之类的，再放上大量二级机枪台和一个机枪火焰合成的炮台，这样攻击可近可远。有多的资源就可以在下面装几个电锯用来挖土，因为那个挖掘核心判定也比较奇怪，有些时候不帮你挖土的。 说这么多，我其实也能猜到作者是想用这些限制来平衡游戏难度，但是我游玩的体验就是这种限制让人很难爽起来，而肉鸽游戏最怕的就是build爽不起来，希望作者能想出更好的平衡方法吧。 ----------------------------------------------- 二编 第一章守门的打完了了，然后就告诉你一句门已打开，我是真无语，直接被坑死，那个门就那么一点点大，我把自己全包在炮台里才活下来。结果进不去门。进不去就算了，连拆炮台的时间都不给，直接给你脸上刷一个大怪把你秒了。半个多小时白打，这样很好玩吗？挫败感极强。 看作者做独立游戏不容易，而且挺看中好评率。本来不想给差评的，但我是cdk买的，差评也不影响游戏整体好评率。算是给作者一个警醒吧，之前也看到有人说新手教程就浪费了十五分钟，因为那个f的破坏教程根本没教你破坏特殊建筑需要直接点它（这个也是很莫名奇妙的）。我觉得游戏这种小问题就是非常非常多。像是物品栏里的东西不知道怎么一键全部丢掉；像是丛林区的压力竟然是第一章最大的，非常非常离谱，我大概能猜到作者是想让你把控在丛林区的发育时间，攒够合理的资源就快速下潜前往第二章，但是给人的可操作空间就太小了，有点不按套路来就白打的感觉；又像是掉落物品不能吸取，到一千多米的时候出去捡东西就要承受高概率被砍一刀的风险，不捡根本收入不了资源。

好玩是好玩，但是很多反人类不合理， 【为什么不能隔着建筑物放置结构物品？判定老恶心了】 【很容易从载具上掉下深井，然后就一堆怪，载具下不来就死了】 【怪太多了吧？炮台还会互相遮挡，怪物各种冲撞根本打不了一点】 【地形很恶心啊，怪从四周过来，然后如果有土，就会聚一堆的怪，然后等土没了以后怪杀不完，就恶心死了】 【最恶心的，就是结构链接完全随机，你想调整载具结构，几乎不可能，稍微按错结构就散架变形】 【不能搭建土平台，有时候掉下一个深坑，通过墙壁也无法返回，这种游戏不能踮脚真的跟不会跳一样，巨恶心】 【地图左右纵深太窄，飞船武器完全没有发挥空间，就跟堵塞的水管一样，你参考一下2d潜艇的哪个游戏，怪物濒临，至少给武器开火的范围，这个竖井整个把船卡住，怪物从土里挖过来，能打到的时候就没了啊】 【可购买的物品太少，结构块和推进器少的一b，悬浮球也少，基本上每次都是小牛拉大车】 我很擅长玩物理建造类的游戏，但是你这游戏我失误率极高，是那种游戏设计上的问题。 目前能上手这游戏的我说实话真的个位数的都难吧

This is one of those games that I really want to like. I've made it partway through chapter 2. I love the core concept: A roguelike where you have the opportunity to build a "ship" from a bunch of basic parts to defend against incoming swarms and eventually fight bosses; placement of turrets, walls, and traversal nodes matter and have gameplay effects. I like the "alchemic turret" system, where you can combine different turrets to find cool and powerful effects. I like the horrory atmosphere, how a bunch of enemies have different behaviors that you have to learn and don't get handheld/preached about. The trap limo train is crazy. And of course I like BEHOLD! THE MAN! Frankly, I like most things about the game... except the usability, and unfortunately that turns the whole review negative because it bleeds into every mechanical aspect of the game. -As far as 2d platforming goes, the physics aren't great. It doesn't seem very consistent whether you'll ramp off of a piece of ankle-high terrain or get completely stuck on it. Sometimes running into a block will destroy it and slide you off of your ledge, sometimes nothing will happen. Walljumps feel really inconsistent. Grappling inertia doesn't feel intuitive or consistent. -Placing a turret puts it into the world, and if it's near something it can build on, it'll send out legs to attach after half a second. During this half-second, it's subject to gravity, so it'll fall a bit before latching on. That's fine, I can account for that, but then it'll only latch a single leg, using the inertia from gravity to swing left or right, then latch the second leg onto what you originally placed it next to... so in practice, it's very rare that you get to place something where you wanted to place it. -To reposition turrets, you'll right click on them, which disengages the leg latches and re-engages them after a second, but sometimes it doesn't work, sometimes it'll disengage a turret that you're not even close to, sometimes it won't re-engage, sometimes it'll re-engage on some other piece of random debris floating around and now that's stuck to your ship too unless you can manage to drive away during the re-engage time, but then you risk the turret not re-engaging at all and you have to exit your ship and jump on it to bump it over. Also I mentioned that doing this involves right clicking... well that's also your "dig" button, so sometimes you'll dig through a bit of terrain, but if you're too close to your ship, you might disengage a turret and mess everything up. -If you're shooting something to the left of your screen, you'll naturally move the mouse over there, but the game pseudo-pauses if you move it too close to the edge. Since it's basically a pause, it doesn't get you killed and it doesn't mess up the game, it's just really annoying. I'm a kind of player that rams my face into challenge; soloing every everdark sovereign (so far) in Nightreign, getting a top-10 global leaderboard time on Neon White's Hell Rush (though it's been so long, I imagine more people have beat my time by now), getting V-rank on a few VVVVVV sections, getting Grandmaster/Celestial rank on a couple esports titles. My issues have nothing to do with difficulty; I'd be happy to get good if it were a matter of that, as I've done for many other games in the past. These are just annoying, un-fun mechanical blunders that feel like roadblocks that show up when I want to engage with the otherwise excellent game concept. I'd be more than happy to come back to the game if these were fixed or made more consistent in function.

The walls are too brittle, often the connection is broken, the entire turret structure is torn apart, and there are too few level 3 towers, and they can't be upgraded wirelessly. I have a suggestion, why not start with a mini modular core (like a spaceship or a mobile base hub), so that I can add turrets, walls, etc. to each module, just like the blueprint of the spaceship mobile base, it will not be as ugly as it is now, more tidy, and then this core can be upgraded so that there is more space for construction. 墙太脆了，经常连接处一断，整个炮塔构架四分五裂，另外3级塔太少了吧，还不能无线升级。 提个建议，为什么不能开局给个迷你模块化核心（类似，宇宙飞船或者移动基地中枢一样），这样我可以在各个模块添加如，炮塔，墙体等，就像飞船移动基地的蓝图一样，不会像现在那样丑，更加的工整，然后让这个核心可以升级，以便于有更大的空间用于建造。
it's like terraria, oxygen not included, and noita had a charmingly lovecraftian bastard child. peak

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44181848/] 【更多适合Steam Deck的好游戏推荐，请关注GPD掌机鉴赏家！】[/url] 现阶段已有神作潜质。 ​​⚙️ 核心亮点：颠覆想象的创意熔炉​​ 1.​​动态生态与移动堡垒的浪漫交响​​ 程序生成的地下世界中，​​生物群落形成捕食链​​（如将敌对生物引向天敌群体可借刀杀人），但生态规则完全依赖玩家试错摸索。 ​​自由建造移动堡垒​​的设定堪称神来之笔：从真空吸尘器起步，逐步组装搭载钻头、悬浮引擎、迫击炮的战争机器，在怪潮涌来时躲在自建装甲内安全感爆棚。 2.​​炼金炮塔与进化路线的策略深度​​ ​​炮塔融合系统​​允许玩家组合出无人机工厂、激光栅栏等独特防御工事，但合成公式需反复试错且无蓝图指引。 ​​六大流派构筑​​（炮塔流/无敌金刚流等）赋予重复游玩价值，清洁机器人进化为"灭霸级女仆"的成长曲线充满戏剧张力。 3.末日叙事与黑色幽默的化学反应​​ 科技狂人拖拽星球撞向太阳的荒诞背景中，​​清洁机器人执念于"干净的家"​​ 的动机既滑稽又悲壮，女仆购物时钱不够发出的蠢萌B音效成为高压中的解压剂。 ​​⚠️ 致命痛点：天才创意与反人类设计的撕裂​​ 1.建造系统：物理引擎的背叛者​​ 结构块连接判定玄学，​​调整载具时频繁散架变形​​； 竖井式地图​​左右纵深过窄​​，炮塔常被墙体或自身载具遮挡无法开火； ​​无法搭建土平台​​，坠落深坑后无垫脚逃生手段，堪称2D版"膝盖中箭"[citation:玩家反馈]。 2.生存体验：绝望的资源枷锁​​ 初始背包仅4格，​​材料/武器/弹药混放​​致临战切换手忙脚乱； ​​回血机制极度稀缺​​，新人常因"次数制血量系统"暴毙（如满血3次机会用完即死）； 商店物资刷新少，​​推进器与悬浮球等关键部件稀缺​​，后期陷入"小牛拉航母"窘境[citation:玩家反馈]。 3.引导缺失：硬核外衣下的信息黑洞​​ 无地图/雷达，​​深度计是唯一定位工具​​，玩家在重复地形中极易迷失； 生物图鉴缺席，中立生物与敌对种群难以区分，​​200+物品无说明需死记硬背​​； 炮塔合成公式全隐藏，消耗品机制晦涩（如"改锥+废铁=自动炮台"需撞大运发现）。 ​​🔮 未来可期？抢先体验的十字路口​​ 开发者Humanyoyo Studios已回应部分问题： ​​背包扩容​​与​​机器升级系统​​将优化资源管理； ​​噩梦模式​​正在测试动态事件与配方封锁机制，成就党福音； 但​​地图功能/建造判定/图鉴系统​​仍悬而未决[citation:玩家反馈]。 ​​▶️ 购买建议​​ ​​适合​​： ✅ 热衷《泰拉瑞亚》×《FTL》式深度缝合的硬核玩家； ✅ 能忍受10小时学习曲线换取"机械神教"快感的建造狂人； ✅ 偏爱《雨世界》生态叙事的实验主义者。 ​​慎入​​： ❌ 追求流畅体验的休闲玩家； ❌ 晕"肉鸽无存档"者（单局90+分钟）； ❌ 建造物理系统过敏人群。

[h1]挖挖挖，我挖挖挖！一直向下挖！[/h1] 《坠落：金属女仆救世录》这款游戏对地图的“造诣”非常之高，不知道大家有没有玩过这种一直向下挖类型的游戏，它的地图创造能力丝毫不亚于《女巫》，而且还糅合了特别多的其它元素，比如塔防，建造，肉鸽；游戏中的地图和很大一部分肉鸽游戏一样，是比较随机的，而且怪物们的立绘也非常有视觉冲击力，并且虽是地底探险类型游戏，但整体的画面呈现并没有想象中那么“昏暗”，也不会有突然找寻不到主角的情况产生，这一点做的非常不错！ 本作还有着一定的建造构筑元素，这就使得游戏有着很强的策略性，玩家可以通过资源收集来建造一些新式的武器，以便可以向更深处的地底“发起进攻”，本作的难度梯度增长感觉不算太快，个人能够适应，但回血的方式和血条有些“过于肉鸽”，不过目前我还没有体验到这款游戏特别深度的局外成长，感觉每次重开给我带来的正反馈内容并不算是特别的优秀！而且有时感觉这个怪群有点过于多，让我这个密集恐惧症患者非常害怕！ 总体来说，这款游戏的创造力和可玩性都非常优秀，但有时候给我带来的正反馈并不算太多，游戏可以提高一下人物血量或者回血手段来增强一下游戏总体的平衡性，我想这样的话整体内容会更加优秀！ [quote][b]关注→[/b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/32969453/][b]✨大众点评鉴赏家✨[/b][/url] [b]新游速递 | 游戏评测 | 周免资讯[/b] [b]加入→ [/b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/dzdp][b]🎮大众点评交流组🎮[/b][/url] [b]心得交流 | 试玩资格 | 聊天吹水[/b][/quote]

第一章绿球强制保证2个，可以借此实现无限纤维（等同于无限气） 即使连接到结构，球体也会在脱离视野一段时间后重新生成，这导致任何将环境实体连接到结构的做法变得徒劳——玩缝合怪的体型不可能小，到处都是的无法摧毁的藤蔓阻止机械进入很多小地方，迫使主角离开机械，然后机械就会在一瞬间四分五裂 其他实体刷新也只看条件不看探索与否，导致无限刷怪和令人精疲力尽的探索（备双份消耗品不然很难回来） 名义上可以直接从第二章开始，但是一开始就要面临2矿1气的枪炮塔、额外支付净化器的巨大经济劣势（第一章1矿1气，同数据同产品） 而第一章到第二章有一个非常荒谬的小口，和全图无敌的背景肉山，迫使玩家快速放弃装备下沉（初见损失非常惨重） 而到了第一章底部（1500）才会解锁合成炮塔（炼金术），导致初次通关基本上等于必须重开。 如果重复玩，不去第一章farm和搜山检海找购物机，第二章等于凭空少了20个枪炮塔，8个墙体（对，作为同为三基本构造类型的墙体刷新率低得可怜），40个火焰塔（理论上气无限所以炮塔能拿满），以及至少三个祝福、三个升级，属性全面劣势。 虽然灵感好像是有了，但是太缺打磨了。

This game is weird ass ♥♥♥♥, but like binding of isaac weird. Incredibly fun most of the time, but sometimes the jank and general balance can make it super frustrating. This game is not what you think it is. Whatever you have in your head, throw it out. There are plenty of other reviews trying to liken this game to others, and, don't get me wrong, it definitely shares traits with those games but... It's just so strange and different that it isn't really doing it justice or describing it well. Like, sure, you can say it's like Terraria (Calamity mod specifically) and World of Goo and Noita and Carrion and Spelunky but with tons of tower defense genre DNA and also there's Hollow Knight style walljumping oh and it has the Klei artstyle but with steampunk apocalypse themes and surprisingly good dialogue. And the protagonist is a robot anime maid, and the game's developer probably [i]still[/i] listens to Steampunk Giraffe to this day. But... Even babbling all of that out doesn't really capture it? This is a rare, truly unique-feeling game. It's not like, completely original, don't go in expecting that, art is never truly original. But it's taken the DNA of so many other games and mashed it up together with the author's own very unique style and sense of art, while still somehow remaining coherent, that it's hard to say "if you like this, you'll like CleanFall." Someone else said that this game feels like someone took an early '00s flash game on CoolMath.com and turned it into its own complete thing with writing and story and more than just a one-trick gimmick, and that's accurate in the best way. It has that same... Auteur madness that stuff like Motherload or Linerider had. If you like trying new, weird, good food, you should try this game. If you're more of a "I just want more of what I already know I like," you probably won't like it. I really like it.

The game just doesn't make any sense. It's very weird and has a lot of interesting ideas. The main problem though is the dev seems to think it's fun to "discover" how things work. Except he gives you no tools to do that. Ships have buoyancy but there's no way to discover that through the UI. You just sort of have to work it out. That would be fine but it applies to everything. Does this turret do good damage? Who knows? You can only spend hours until you find an enemy with actual health and it fails to kill it. Then your run is done. I've nothing against a game that doesn't hold your hand but this game has too many complicated confusing things in it and goes out of it's way to make them hard to figure out. The result is you spending your time making very little progress and there's no community to work with to discover these things.

What in particular needs to happen in those few more years to make the game worth buying? Thanks for trying out my game! ___________ If I wanted to "expound" upon it I would have initially. But since you have stimulated me in such a gentlemanly fashion I will explain a bit more. I do not feel like the game is worth it at this time. The game feels unfocused and clunky. Why is it impossible to change the angle of walls at the central node after placement, why do the small wall nodes attach to external environment randomly? Why do things have a different amount of "legs", no legs, rigid legs, flexible legs? Why is it called turret alchemy, why are there not more combinations, why is the combination chart the way it is visually that leads you to think there are more combinations? What is the point of the other two classes, why can summons that have a duration be killed? Why do guns suck? Why are you forced to scrap nearly everything to fit through a hole? Should time pause while building so that you can untangle frustrating jank without having to deal with enemies wandering in or the accelerating approach of midnight? Why is the reapers music such a short loop? Because I know that the answer to all these questions and more could be that the game is not finished and because I do not care to check if my uninsightful complaints are addressed in potential future plans. To be fair to the game and my time I only wished to convey in as few words as possible that, in my opinion, the game is not worth it at this time but perhaps when it is finished it will be. Also, while you could not have known, given my experience with early access games, I cannot convey how profound an expression of optimism my initial review is.

CleanFall is an inventive survival roguelike that blends exploration, crafting, base building, and tower defense into a surprisingly cohesive experience. Developed and published by Humanyoyo, the game places players in a dangerous underground world where survival depends not only on combat skills but also on creativity, planning, and resource management. Rather than following a straightforward progression system, it encourages experimentation, allowing players to forge their own path through a constantly changing environment filled with threats and opportunities. One of the game's most appealing features is its emphasis on freedom. Players are given a vast array of tools and construction options that allow them to shape the world around them. Resources gathered during expeditions can be transformed into weapons, defensive structures, machinery, and mobile platforms capable of handling increasingly dangerous situations. The satisfaction comes not from unlocking predetermined upgrades but from discovering effective designs and strategies through trial and error. This approach gives every play session a sense of individuality, as different players may tackle the same challenges in completely different ways. Exploration plays a major role in the overall experience. The underground environments are procedurally generated, ensuring that each run offers new terrain layouts, hidden resources, and unexpected encounters. Digging through the world becomes more than a means of transportation; it is a core gameplay mechanic that allows players to create shortcuts, establish defensive positions, and uncover valuable materials. The deeper players venture, the greater the rewards become, but so do the risks. This constant balance between greed and caution creates an engaging sense of tension throughout the adventure. Combat is built around more than simply fighting enemies directly. CleanFall places significant emphasis on preparation and engineering. Turrets, traps, automated defenses, and various crafted devices can be combined to create powerful defensive systems capable of dealing with large enemy waves. The day-and-night cycle further enhances this dynamic, as periods of exploration are often followed by intense survival scenarios that test the effectiveness of a player's preparations. Success frequently depends on how well players have utilized their resources and designed their defenses rather than on reflexes alone. The crafting and construction systems are among the game's strongest elements. Building mobile bases and customizable combat platforms adds a layer of strategic depth rarely seen in similar survival titles. Players can transform simple vehicles into heavily armed machines capable of traversing hazardous environments while providing protection against hostile creatures. This mechanic ties together exploration, resource gathering, and combat in a satisfying way, making progression feel meaningful and rewarding. Visually, the game adopts a distinctive hand-drawn style that complements its mysterious underground setting. The environments are filled with personality, and the various creatures inhabiting the depths contribute to an atmosphere that feels both adventurous and threatening. While the presentation may not compete with large-budget productions in terms of technical complexity, the artistic direction succeeds in creating a memorable identity and reinforces the game's sense of discovery. As an Early Access release, CleanFall still shows signs of ongoing development. Certain systems can feel overwhelming for newcomers, and some balance issues may become apparent as players experiment with different builds and playstyles. The depth that makes the game compelling can also create a steep learning curve, especially when dealing with advanced crafting mechanics and resource management. However, these shortcomings are largely offset by the game's ambition and the strong foundation already in place. What makes CleanFall stand out is its ability to combine several genres without losing focus. It successfully merges survival gameplay, roguelike progression, engineering creativity, and defensive strategy into a package that feels fresh and engaging. The game rewards curiosity and experimentation, encouraging players to constantly refine their designs and adapt to new challenges. Even when setbacks occur, the process of learning and improving remains enjoyable. For players who enjoy sandbox survival games with deep building systems and a strong emphasis on player creativity, CleanFall offers a rewarding and distinctive experience. Its combination of procedural exploration, customizable vehicles, defensive construction, and strategic resource management creates a gameplay loop that remains entertaining for long stretches. Although further refinement will undoubtedly improve the experience, the current version already demonstrates considerable potential and provides a solid foundation for future growth. Rating: 8/10
